caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular, shrine-like frame with a slanted roof, colored predominantly in shades of red, pink, and purple. Inside the frame are several stylized, human-like figures with angular faces and pointed crowns or headdresses, each encased in a dark, almond-shaped outline, reminiscent of flower petals or mandorlas. The largest figure, positioned in the center, wears a red robe with yellow and gold stripes and stands with hands together. Smaller, similarly dressed figures occupy the four corners, each enclosed within their own almond-shaped outline and standing on red, oval platforms. At the top, three busts of figures, each with distinct headdresses and facial expressions, are arranged in a horizontal row. At the bottom center, beneath the main figure, a smaller human figure with wings appears to be supporting or holding up the central figure, surrounded by green-and-red floral or leafy motifs. Additional green, red, and black abstract floral shapes are dispersed between the figures. The background is a light tan or cream color, and the outlines and details are rendered in black. The roof displays a dark, abstract motif, possibly of birds or flames, and there is a small number “32” at the bottom left corner outside the frame.
title: Plate 32: Our Lady of Guadalupe: From Portfolio "Spanish Colonial Designs of New Mexico"
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
